19692.etyen:
Compound of giss (“G-sharp”) + moll (“minor”), literally “G-sharp minor”.
The first element giss (“G-sharp”) is formed from the note name G (“G”) with -iss (“sharp”); the suffix continues German -is (“sharp”). The second element moll (“minor”) is through German Moll (“minor”) from Medieval Latin Medieval Latin molle (“soft”), the neuter of Latin Latin mollis (“soft, mild”), from Proto-Italic Proto-Italic *moldus (“soft”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European Proto-Indo-European *ml̥dús (“soft, weak”). The further derivation of the Proto-Indo-European word is disputed.

1001452.etyen:
Internationalism, ultimately from Ancient Greek Καλλιστώ (Kallistṓ, “Kallisto; the most beautiful one”). The Ancient Greek name is from κᾰ́λλῐστος (kắllĭstos, “most beautiful”) + -ώ (-ṓ, “female given-name suffix”), literally “the most beautiful one”. The name was rendered in Latin as Callistō. The Norwegian spelling Kallisto reflects the Greek form, while Callisto is used in Norwegian for the moon of Jupiter named after her. The asteroid 204 Kallisto is likewise named after the mythological Kallisto.
Compare the parallel adaptations Danish Kallisto, Swedish Kallisto, German Kallisto, Finnish
